O1
How this course works
Visual route
No matching instructor video is assigned for this topic. Use the worked explanation and diagrams below.
What you are learning
You will separate recognising an explanation from being able to do the task yourself. Reading is
useful, but a data job also requires producing a result, checking it and explaining it. Here,
practice starts in the first module; you will not wait until the end to use what you learn.
Words before we use them
Word
Meaning in this course
Guided example
Work you do while following the book.
Independent attempt
Your own work with the answer closed. An unfinished attempt still counts as
an honest attempt.
Evidence
Your saved answer, file or result showing what you actually did.
Review
Reading the worked solution after saving your attempt.
Changed retry
A different example testing the same skill.
Mastered
You can do a changed task, check it and explain why the answer works.
Follow with me once
Imagine the task is to copy a file without losing the original. Riya watches a demonstration. She
now recognises Copy and Paste, but has not shown that she can use them. Next she copies the
book's file while following each click. That is guided practice. Finally she closes the book, copies a
different file, reopens both copies and proves only her working copy changed. That is
independent evidence.
A wrong first answer is useful information. If Riya used Cut and the original disappeared, the
repair is to understand Copy versus Move, restore the source, and retry with a different file.
Reading the whole module again would not directly repair that one mistake.
What to do today
Open Notepad using Windows Start. Write six short lines: learn, follow, try alone, check, review
and repair, changed retry and explain. Save O1_course_route.txt in Documents/Analyst_Lab
using the Start Here instructions. The six lines are a memory aid; explaining what you do at each
stage matters more than reciting the exact words.

Files, folders and safe data handling
Visual route
No matching instructor video is assigned for this topic. Use the worked explanation and diagrams below.
What you are learning
A file can have the same name in two different folders. You must know which copy you are
editing. This lesson creates a safe place for all later work and proves that you can recover from a
mistake without damaging the only source.
Words before we use them
Word
Plain-English meaning
File / folder
One saved item / a container holding items.
Path
The address of an item, including its containing folders.
Extension
The ending such as .txt or .pdf, which helps identify the file type.
Raw input
The original data received for the exercise. Preserve it.
Working copy
A separate copy you may change.
Output / evidence
A result you produce / proof of what you did and checked.
Original in raw_data
Orders.txt
Keep this record unchanged.
Copy in processed_data
Orders.txt
Edit only this copy.
Copy
Same filename. Different folders. Two separate files.
Close and reopen both; check their paths and first records.
Restore a damaged raw copy from the untouched course input.
See the folder map
Each row below is a folder inside Documents/Analyst_Lab. The package's Practice folder supplies
starter files; your Analyst_Lab holds your own attempts.

Follow with me on Windows
1. Press Windows+E to open File Explorer. Open Documents, then Analyst_Lab from O1. Use New
> Folder, or Ctrl+Shift+N, to create each of the five named folders. Create them inside
Analyst_Lab, not five unrelated places.
2. Turn on file endings. In Windows 11 use View > Show > File name extensions. In the older
ribbon layout use View > File name extensions. This changes what names you see, not the files'
contents.
3. In the extracted course, open C1/M00/Practice/Inputs. Select Orders.txt once. Press Ctrl+C. Go
to Analyst_Lab/raw_data and press Ctrl+V. Both the package input and your raw copy should
remain.
4. Select raw_data/Orders.txt, press Ctrl+C, open processed_data and press Ctrl+V. Copy creates
another item. Cut (Ctrl+X) followed by Paste moves the item; do not use it here.
5. Double-click processed_data/Orders.txt to open it in Notepad. Change only the first order's
Region from East to West. Press Ctrl+S. Close it. Open raw_data/Orders.txt: the first order must
still say East. Open the working copy: it must say West.
6. In Notepad create documentation/source_note.txt. Write "Orders.txt is fictional practice data.
One record describes one order. I changed Region only in the working copy." Move
O1_course_route.txt into documentation now; moving your own answer to organise it is fine.
7. Close File Explorer, reopen it and locate both files again. The address bar should show
raw_data for the original and processed_data for your edited copy. A Recent files shortcut alone
does not prove which copy you opened.
Check the result
The original lists O1001, East, 20. The working copy lists O1001, West, 20. The other records
remain unchanged. Save a screenshot showing each file and its location if possible, or write the
two full paths and first records in documentation/O2_files.txt. Do not claim a screenshot proves
unchanged bytes; it shows the visible content you inspected.

If something goes wrong
If raw_data is empty, you likely moved the file. Copy Orders.txt again from the untouched
package, then make a new working copy. If Notepad asks Save As when editing a supplied file,
check you extracted the ZIP and are in your own writable folder. If a file becomes Orders.txt.txt,

For a screenshot, press Windows+Shift+S, select the area, then save the capture in screenshots.
Some Windows versions put the capture on the clipboard first; open Paint, paste it, then save a
PNG. Screenshots supplement saved work; they do not replace the actual file.

Visual route

What you are learning

F1
What does a data analyst actually
do?
Watch first
1. Alex The Analyst - What Does a Data Analyst Do: Meetings, Data, Excel, SQL
Retained instructor video. Optional visual, no verified bounded range. Its original page and exact title were
corroborated on 17 September 2026; full playback and runtime were not verified. Use the role overview, then return
to the eight-stage example. This is not a task-specific demonstration of our fictional shop.
Pause to connect the demonstration to the example below. Use the printed stop time when a bounded range is
given; longer recordings remain available for reference.
Start with a familiar shop
A shop owner says, "Sales look bad. Make a chart." An analyst helps turn that concern into a
question that data can answer, checks the answer, and explains what decision it can support.
Excel and SQL are tools for that work. The reasoning comes first.
Words before we use them
Word
Meaning
Stakeholder
Someone who needs, uses or is affected by the answer.
Business question
A question connected to a decision, such as which products to investigate.
Hypothesis
A possible explanation to test, not an established cause.
Validation
Checks on the data, calculation and meaning of the result.
Finding
A statement supported by the analysed evidence.

Contents
Follow with me: the shop request
Stage
What the analyst does
Problem
Record the owner's concern about sales and the decision to prioritise
product reviews.
Clarify
Ask whether sales means orders, units or money, and compared with which
period.
Data
Request order date, product, quantity, price, status and the approved
return rules.
Prepare
Preserve the original, inspect missing values and identify duplicate records.
Analyse
Compare the agreed measure by product for the two approved periods.
Validate
Check counted orders, totals and included dates against the defined scope.
Communicate
Explain the observed change, exclusions and remaining uncertainty.
Decision support
Offer evidence for the owner to prioritise investigation. The owner chooses
the action.
For a small fictional example, suppose the approved completed-order count is 100 last month
and 80 this month for the same shop. The count fell by 20 orders, or 20/100 = 20% relative to
last month. That calculation does not show why it fell. A price increase, missing export or holiday
closure is something to investigate. The analyst must not invent an explanation to make the
answer sound confident.
Try it yourself
A support manager says, "Customers are unhappy. Tell me what is going on." Write one useful
action for each of the eight stages. No numerical complaint data is supplied, so do not invent a
trend. Label any proposed period or metric as a proposal. Save documentation/F1_workflow.txt
before review.
Changed retry
A warehouse manager says, "Late deliveries are getting worse." Repeat the eight stages with a
different decision and requested fields. Explain why delivery records alone may show lateness
without proving traffic caused it.
Ready to continue
You can describe the workflow without naming a particular application and can separate an
observed change from an unsupported cause. Next: F2, where you learn to make the question
precise.

F2
From vague request to analytical
question
Visual route
No matching instructor video is assigned for this topic. Use the worked explanation and diagrams below.
Why a precise question helps
"Complaints are high lately" leaves several blanks. High compared with last week, last year or a
target? Complaints from which customers? Does "complaints" mean messages or distinct
complaint cases? Different choices can produce different answers while both calculations look
correct.
Five questions to ask
Handle
Example clarification
Decision
What action will this result help you choose?
Comparison
Which earlier period or approved target should we compare with?
Scope
Which store, channel, team or customer group belongs in the analysis?
Time
Which dates, date field and timezone define the period?
Meaning
What exactly counts as a complaint, order or cancellation?
A scope is a boundary. An assumption is a temporary belief still needing confirmation. A
confirmed fact comes from the scenario or an actual answer from the responsible person. Writing
"I assume" makes a choice visible; it does not turn it into an approved business rule.
Follow with me once
The original request is "Sales are down." Imagine the owner then confirms: North region; online
completed orders; August 2026 versus August 2025; order date; gross merchandise amount
before refunds; decide which product categories to investigate first. These are additional fictional
replies for this worked example, not facts about a real shop.
A bounded question is: "For North online completed orders dated in August 2026, which product
categories had the largest decrease in gross merchandise amount compared with August 2025?"
It identifies the measure, eligible records, period, comparison and output grouping. It asks where
the decrease occurred. It does not claim a price or campaign caused it.
If refund data becomes available later, do not silently switch to net sales. That would answer a
different question. Record the changed definition and obtain agreement first.

F3
Metrics and KPIs
Visual route
No matching instructor video is assigned for this topic. Use the worked explanation and diagrams below.
Words before we use them
A metric is a defined measurement. A KPI is a metric selected as especially important to an
objective. A target is the desired level. "On-time rate" is the metric; "at least 90%" might be its
approved target. Adding a target does not explain who counts as on time.
For a percentage, the denominator is the eligible group being measured. The numerator is the
part of that same group meeting the condition. Divide the numerator by the denominator and
multiply by 100. If the eligible group is empty, report "not applicable: no eligible records", not
Follow with me using five deliveries
For this fictional training example only, the owner approves: use completed deliveries in the
period, exclude cancelled deliveries, count delivery at or before the promised time as on time, no
grace minutes, and use actual delivery date. All times below are on the same day in the same
timezone.
Delivery
Status

time?

The eligible denominator is D1, D2, D3 and D5: four deliveries. The numerator is D1, D2 and D5:
three. The rate is 3/4 x 100 = 75%. Dividing by all five records would give 60%, which answers a
different question because a cancelled record is included.
You cannot silently exclude a Completed delivery with a missing delivered time and announce a
complete rate. That is a data-quality exception. Record the unknown, investigate it and follow an
approved handling rule. Removing hard cases can make performance look better than it is.

A training programme approves: first attempts only; exclude cancelled bookings; pass at a score

F4
Grain and required data
Visual route
No matching instructor video is assigned for this topic. Use the worked explanation and diagrams below.
First understand rows and fields
A table stores records in rows and attributes in columns. A field is one named attribute, such as
OrderID or Region. The heading row gives field names and is not a data record. A data type
describes the kind of value: text, a number, a date/time or a true/false value. An identifier may
look numeric but is a label; averaging order IDs would have no useful business meaning. Missing
means unknown or unavailable here, not automatically zero.
Grain is the sentence "one row represents one ...". Say it before counting. Three lines of products
may belong to one order. Counting those lines as three orders gives the wrong answer.
Follow with me: an order and its lines
Orders has one row per OrderID:
OrderID
Region
Shipping
East
West
OrderLines has one row per product line within an order:
OrderID
LineNo
Product
Line amount
Pen
Book
Bag
File
OrderID is unique in Orders. In OrderLines the pair OrderID + LineNo identifies a line; neither
column alone is unique. Repeated O1001 is legitimate because there are three different product
lines. A key is an identifier or combination expected to identify one record. A foreign key points
to a parent record, so it may repeat on child records.
Imagine attaching the order's shipping fee to every line. O1001's 20 appears three times and
O1002's 30 once. Summing now gives 20+20+20+30 = 90, although actual shipping is 20+30 =
50. The data did not gain another shipment; the display repeated an order-level value. Count
orders from the order table or count distinct OrderID; total shipping once per order. You will
implement these choices in SQL later.

One shipping fee: 20
Three product lines
Correct shipping total: 20

Line 1: shipping 20
Line 2: shipping 20
Line 3: shipping 20
Attach
Adding copied shipping values gives 60 for the same order.
Keep order-level shipping separate from line-level amounts.

F5
Data quality
Visual route
No matching instructor video is assigned for this topic. Use the worked explanation and diagrams below.
Check before changing
Data quality asks whether the data is fit for the intended answer. A tidy table can still have
missing orders or wrong dates. Five useful checks are completeness, uniqueness, validity,
consistency and timeliness. Accuracy adds another question: does the stored value match what
actually happened? Passing a format rule alone does not prove accuracy.
Follow with me: delivery records
Suppose we must report August completed deliveries. The approved grain is one record per
DeliveryID; required fields include status, promised time, delivered time and hub. The owner
confirms an export complete through 31 August, 23:59, local time. That export coverage must be
checked; a recent LastUpdatedAt on one row does not prove every expected record arrived.
Check
Concrete test and why it matters
Completeness
Count Completed deliveries without PromisedAt or DeliveredAt; their
on-time result is unknown.
Uniqueness
Find repeated DeliveryID in the summary table; duplicate records may
inflate the rate's counts.
Validity
Check allowed statuses and whether DeliveredAt is before an impossible
prerequisite such as order creation, if that field is supplied.
Consistency
Check whether North and NORTH refer to one hub and whether all
timestamps use the agreed timezone.
Timeliness
Confirm export coverage through the cutoff with the source owner and
expected records; a file downloaded today can contain old data.
For every failure, write observation, possible impact and next action. Example: "D17 is
Completed but DeliveredAt is blank; on-time classification is unknown; request the source
correction and flag the affected count." Do not replace a missing time with midnight or delete
D17 merely to finish.
Early delivery is allowed. DeliveredAt before PromisedAt can mean good performance. An
unusual amount can also be real. The rule needs meaning, not just a comparison sign.

Open Practice/Inputs/Appointments.txt in Notepad. Grain is one appointment per AppointmentID.

The book tells you what to look for so you can practise interpreting failures. Do not delete rows.
Save documentation/F5_quality.txt.

Now consider Orders.txt for cancellation-rate analysis. The approved grain is one order; fields

file is insufficient for this analysis and request the missing fields. Do not manufacture their

Contents
F6
Analysis validation and the complete
analyst brief
Visual route
No matching instructor video is assigned for this topic. Use the worked explanation and diagrams below.
Bring the ideas together
An analyst brief is a short plan that keeps the question, measure, data and checks aligned. You
can write it in plain text. It prevents a technically correct calculation from answering the wrong
question. Use four sections: Problem; Measure + Data; Trust Checks; Done + Defence.
A reconciliation compares your result with a separate trusted reference under matching
definitions and scope. A sanity check looks for impossible or surprising results. Neither replaces
investigating an actual discrepancy. A Definition of Done lists observable conditions for accepting
the work.
Follow with me: subscriptions
For this fictional example, a training-business owner confirms the task: identify September
renewal cohorts needing follow-up. One row in Practice/Inputs/Renewals.txt represents one
subscription due for renewal. Every row is due during September; each has Region, AmountDue,
Status and PaidAmount. The owner approves Status=Renewed as success, Cancelled as not
renewed, and both statuses in the due cohort. These are exercise rules, not a universal churn
definition.
Section
Worked brief
Problem
Compare renewal rate by region for September due subscriptions; help
prioritise customer follow-up.
Measure + Data
Renewed subscriptions divided by all subscriptions due in September, by
region. One source row per SubscriptionID; one result row per Region for
the month.
Trust Checks
Check unique IDs, allowed statuses, required region, nonnegative amounts,
due-cohort coverage and compatible labels. Count each subscription once.
Done + Defence
Publish numerator, denominator, rate, exclusions and matching receipt
controls; flag uncertainty; save source and calculation. No claim about why
customers cancelled.

WORKED PATTERN Suppose you return tomorrow during F3. In documentation/Next_Action.txt
you previously wrote: "F3 first attempt saved as F3_metric.txt; I could not decide who belongs in
the denominator. Next: open F3 in M00_Worked_Answers.pdf, then retry without it." You can now

attempt's filename, one unresolved issue, the review section and the new retry. In this course a
useful progress note can be four lines; you do not need another long notebook.
F1 | What does a data analyst actually do?
WORKED PATTERN For a small fictional example, suppose the approved completed-order count is
100 last month and 80 this month for the same shop. The count fell by 20 orders, or 20/100 =
20% relative to last month. That calculation does not show why it fell. A price increase, missing
export or holiday closure is something to investigate. The analyst must not invent an explanation
to make the answer sound confident.
CHANGED RETRY A warehouse manager says, "Late deliveries are getting worse." Repeat the
eight stages with a different decision and requested fields. Explain why delivery records alone
may show lateness without proving traffic caused it.
F2 | From vague request to analytical question
WORKED PATTERN The original request is "Sales are down." Imagine the owner then confirms:
North region; online completed orders; August 2026 versus August 2025; order date; gross
merchandise amount before refunds; decide which product categories to investigate first. These
are additional fictional replies for this worked example, not facts about a real shop. A bounded
question is: "For North online completed orders dated in August 2026, which product categories
had the largest decrease in gross merchandise amount compared with August 2025?" It
identifies the measure, eligible records, period, comparison and output grouping. It asks where
the decrease occurred. It does not claim a price or campaign caused it. If refund data becomes
available later, do not silently switch to net sales. That would answer a different question. Record
the changed definition and obtain agreement first.
WHY "Complaints are high lately" leaves several blanks. High compared with last week, last year
or a target? Complaints from which customers? Does "complaints" mean messages or distinct
complaint cases? Different choices can produce different answers while both calculations look
correct.
CHANGED RETRY Use "Returns are getting worse." Propose a different comparison and time
period. Explain how a count of return requests differs from a percentage of delivered orders
returned. Mark the returns definition and denominator as needing agreement if not supplied.

Contents
F3 | Metrics and KPIs
WORKED PATTERN For this fictional training example only, the owner approves: use completed
deliveries in the period, exclude cancelled deliveries, count delivery at or before the promised
time as on time, no grace minutes, and use actual delivery date. All times below are on the same
day in the same timezone. The eligible denominator is D1, D2, D3 and D5: four deliveries. The
numerator is D1, D2 and D5: three. The rate is 3/4 x 100 = 75%. Dividing by all five records
would give 60%, which answers a different question because a cancelled record is included. You
cannot silently exclude a Completed delivery with a missing delivered time and announce a
complete rate. That is a data-quality exception. Record the unknown, investigate it and follow an
approved handling rule. Removing hard cases can make performance look better than it is.
CHANGED RETRY A training programme approves: first attempts only; exclude cancelled
bookings; pass at a score of 60 or above. First-attempt scores are 60, 75, 45 and 59. A cancelled
booking has no score, and a second attempt scores 90. Calculate the first-attempt pass rate and
explain why the other two records do not enter the denominator. Then explain the result if there
are no eligible first attempts.
F4 | Grain and required data
WORKED PATTERN Orders has one row per OrderID: OrderLines has one row per product line
within an order: OrderID is unique in Orders. In OrderLines the pair OrderID + LineNo identifies a
line; neither column alone is unique. Repeated O1001 is legitimate because there are three
different product lines. A key is an identifier or combination expected to identify one record. A
foreign key points to a parent record, so it may repeat on child records. Imagine attaching the
order's shipping fee to every line. O1001's 20 appears three times and O1002's 30 once.
Summing now gives 20+20+20+30 = 90, although actual shipping is 20+30 = 50. The data did
not gain another shipment; the display repeated an order-level value. Count orders from the
order table or count distinct OrderID; total shipping once per order. You will implement these
choices in SQL later. For a monthly regional summary, result grain is one row per region and
month. To build it you need an approved date basis, region, eligible status rules and the
measures at their proper grains. "All columns" is not a data requirement. Name what the
question needs.
CHANGED RETRY Use Products (ProductID, Category), Orders (OrderID, OrderDate, Status) and
OrderLines (OrderID, LineNo, ProductID, Quantity). State each key/grain and the required fields
for monthly units sold by category. Explain why repeated ProductID in OrderLines does not
automatically identify bad records. Do not invent SQL syntax; plain-language reasoning is the
task.

Contents
F5 | Data quality
WORKED PATTERN Suppose we must report August completed deliveries. The approved grain is
one record per DeliveryID; required fields include status, promised time, delivered time and hub.
The owner confirms an export complete through 31 August, 23:59, local time. That export
coverage must be checked; a recent LastUpdatedAt on one row does not prove every expected
record arrived. For every failure, write observation, possible impact and next action. Example:
"D17 is Completed but DeliveredAt is blank; on-time classification is unknown; request the
source correction and flag the affected count." Do not replace a missing time with midnight or
delete D17 merely to finish. Early delivery is allowed. DeliveredAt before PromisedAt can mean
good performance. An unusual amount can also be real. The rule needs meaning, not just a
comparison sign.
CHANGED RETRY Now consider Orders.txt for cancellation-rate analysis. The approved grain is
one order; fields required are OrderID, OrderDate, Region, Status and export coverage. Design
one check for each of the five dimensions. The tiny Orders.txt used in O2 lacks OrderDate and
Status: state that the file is insufficient for this analysis and request the missing fields. Do not
manufacture their values. An honest blocked analysis is a valid result.
F6 | Analysis validation and the complete analyst brief
WORKED PATTERN For this fictional example, a training-business owner confirms the task:
identify September renewal cohorts needing follow-up. One row in Practice/Inputs/Renewals.txt
represents one subscription due for renewal. Every row is due during September; each has
Region, AmountDue, Status and PaidAmount. The owner approves Status=Renewed as success,
Cancelled as not renewed, and both statuses in the due cohort. These are exercise rules, not a
universal churn definition. North contains S1 Renewed for 100 and S2 Cancelled for 100, with no
payment for S2. South contains S3 Renewed for 200. North renewal rate is 1/2 = 50%; South is
1/1 = 100%; overall is 2/3 = 66.67%. The overall rate is not the simple average of 50% and 100%
(75%) because the region groups have different sizes. The separate training reference in
Renewal_Control.txt says September receipts total 300. PaidAmount totals 100+0+200 = 300,
so receipts reconcile for the supplied same-scope example. AmountDue totals 400 and should
not be forced to equal receipts. The 300 receipt match does not by itself validate the renewal
rate: money and subscription counts are different measures. Two wrong rows can also offset in a
total, so inspect records and rules as well.
CHANGED RETRY A manager next asks, "Why did South cancel?" Write what the supplied file can
show, what it cannot show, and what additional evidence you would request. Do not infer a cause
from the region label or a one-subscription sample. Then open M00_Practice_Guide.pdf for the
FreshNest and BrightBasket combined cases.

MEASURE | Define duration,

Proposed duration per eligible appointment is SeenAt minus CheckInAt in minutes after

record with a missing time cannot silently vanish from the performance story.

threshold before publishing. If the business instead wants percentage waiting beyond a
threshold, define numerator as eligible appointments exceeding the approved threshold and
denominator as the same eligible population, with an explicit rule for unknown outcomes. No
threshold exists in this case. No eligible records means N/A, with the zero count shown. A KPI is
justified if reducing patient waiting is an agreed objective; the label is not automatic.
appointment_summary is one row per AppointmentID. appointment_events is one row per

under the proposed question. Required fields include AppointmentID, Clinic, CheckInAt, SeenAt,

that interval or basis is chosen. Specialty/PatientType are needed only if their breakdown or

Dimension
Check, consequence and action
Completeness
Required Hub and promised/delivered timestamps present for eligible
records. Unknown time prevents classification. Request source correction
and keep affected counts visible.
Uniqueness
Unique DeliveryID in summary and EventID in events. Repeated EventID
suggests duplicate scans; repeated DeliveryID across distinct events can be
valid.
Validity
Timestamps parse, statuses/service levels are approved and chosen rule is
applied consistently. DeliveredAt before PromisedAt can be valid early
delivery; do not label it impossible.
Consistency
Hub names, status mappings, units and timezone rules agree. Use
approved mappings and document timezone conversion.
Timeliness
Source confirms every included hub supplied data through cutoff, including
relevant late status updates. Current file download time is not proof of
coverage.
Manually classify a delivery before the threshold, exactly at it and after it once the threshold is
approved. Use a cross-midnight case to test the chosen week assignment. Numerator IDs must
belong to the denominator; rates must be within 0-100% where defined; group counts must sum
to the detailed scope without duplicated deliveries. Report excluded and unresolved cases
separately.
Network Operations completed counts can reconcile completed deliveries by matching
hub/week/date/status/cutoff. If the service metric includes failed deliveries, its eligible
denominator should not be forced to equal completed counts. Build a separate completed-only
comparison or obtain a broader aligned reference. This count reconciliation cannot prove
timestamp accuracy or the late classification. Sampling source promise and delivery records is
another check. Very long lateness should be investigated, not silently capped.

support
Observable done conditions: approved population/grace/week/timezone definitions; one intended
summary per delivery; missing/invalid and excluded cases reported; boundary and
cross-midnight cases recalculated; per-hub numerator/denominator totals reconcile;
completed-count reference compared under matching rules; preserved inputs and saved result;
descriptive finding with limitations.
Ready to ask questions, profile fields and define the analysis. Not Ready to publish final hub
rates or declare an increasing trend until definitions, periods and observations are available. No
traffic, staffing or customer cause is established.
Defence: a late rate compares late deliveries with the same eligible delivery set. Many events
can legitimately describe one delivery, so scanning activity cannot be used as its denominator. A
completed-count reference checks completed counts, not every possible service denominator. A
chosen rate's meaning is part of correctness, not just its arithmetic.
